title: Boson-star microlensing
model_status: Hypothetical dark lens; numerical reconstruction using the authors’ tabulated profile, not a new equilibrium solution.

source_papers.title: Crispim Romao & Croon (2024; revised 2025), Microlensing signatures of extended dark objects using machine learning
source_papers.used_for: Equations 4–6, 9 and authors’ numerical projected-mass tables; finite-source disk extension added here.

source_papers.title: Croon, McKeen & Raj (2020), Gravitational microlensing by dark matter in extended structures
source_papers.used_for: Appendix A: source of mass profiles; non-self-interacting nonrelativistic boson ground state, or NFW profile truncated at 100 scale radii.

equations.lens_equation: signed source radius y(r)=r-m(r)/r; all radii in point-mass Einstein-radius units
equations.finite_source_implementation: Afs=integral_0^infty r*angular_length(y(r),u,rho) dr/(pi*rho^2), from surface-brightness conservation; all image annuli included

assumed_parameters_origin: Illustrative scenario choices, not measurements, posterior estimates, or universal class properties; exceptions identified in paper_constraints.

derived_model_parameters.finite_source_extension: Uniform-disk image-area integral; paper uses point sources. No wave optics.

limitations: One illustrative geometry and parameter choice, not the population distribution or a prediction of discovery rate.
Gaussian noise is illustrative; stellar variability, blending variability, quality flags, gaps and extraction systematics are absent.
No identity, mass or primordial origin can be established from morphological similarity alone.
Profile family and interpolation are fixed; self-interactions and other density profiles can change the curve.
Paper simulated point sources; this uniform finite-source extension is independently derived and checked against analytic point-lens limits.
Einstein time and dimensionless radii are scenario parameters; mass, particle mass, distances and velocities are not separately inferred.
Geometric optics only; lens transparency assumed. Caustics can also arise from ordinary binary lenses.

noise_free_curve.note: Display table thinned to roughly 12000 points; exposure integration used the full internal grid.

numerics.time_integration: Boxcar from cumulative trapezoidal integral; <= exposure/32 internal timestep
numerics.source_surface_brightness: Uniform disk for lensing; no limb darkening
numerics.noise: Independent Gaussian, fixed seed; not a realistic KBonus noise model
numerics.photometric_band: Achromatic geometric-lensing approximation; TZO is an uncalibrated relative-flux proxy

classification_limit: For proposing follow-up hypotheses only; neither a detection model nor validation. Similar ordinary objects and instrumental effects must be tested independently.

mass_profile_input.interpretation: Projected cylindrical mass, NOT three-dimensional enclosed mass. Table outer radius is the same scale used by the authors’ simulate.py; do not rename it r90.
mass_profile_input.interpolation: Even cubic spline with origin (0,0); mass fraction set to 1 outside the tabulated outer radius.
